Subject: MAP: performance lab & action timeline (TTFT / load profiles)

Jordan — kicking off the MAP item for the performance lab we discussed on the call. Goal is to validate SLAs for your production-like workload and agree close milestones so procurement can finish the PO by mid‑August. High-level ask: run a joint lab that verifies TTFT, tail latency, and sustained throughput under your expected concurrency profile.

Proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- TTFT: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Token throughput: sustain 500 rps (requests/sec) for 60m with average prompt length ~100 tokens
- Spike handling: tolerate a 5-minute ramp to 2,500 rps with graceful queueing and <2% reject rate
- Concurrency: client-side concurrency up to 250; server-side queue depth and backpressure behavior observed and documented

We attached our load harness and a MAP template for milestones. Can you share a sample traffic profile (CSV) and a preferred 2–3 hour window for the lab next week? We’ll bring Karthik (serving/runtime) and Neha (CS/close) to the run.

Attachments: redwood-load-harness-v1.tar.gz, redwood-map-template.xlsx

Planned test matrix (all runs will include request/response token counts and GV metrics):
1) Baseline functional check (10m) — 50 rps, short prompts (<=64 tokens) — validate instrumentation
2) Sustained steady profile (60m) — 500 rps sustained, prompt distribution per your CSV (median ~100 tokens)
3) Spike stress test (5m ramp to peak) — ramp 0 -> 2,500 rps over 90s, hold 5m, ramp down — observe queue growth and reject behavior
4) Context-heavy TTFT probe (15m) — sporadic long-context (>=2k tokens) at 80 rps to see cache/KV warm-up impact

Metrics to capture: TTFT (time to first token), p50/p95/p99 latency per request, tokens/sec, GPU util, scheduler queue length, rejected/429s, e2e tail latencies including network.

Operational notes / planned tuning:
- We’ll test with (a) client-side concurrency 250 and (b) client-side concurrency 100 to contrast queueing patterns.
- Suggest enabling prefix KV caching for the context-heavy probe.
- We'll also test two rate-limit policies: fixed-leaky bucket and adaptive token-bucket to compare latency vs reject rate.

Attachment: proposed-rate-limit-config.txt (contains server-side rate-limit templates)

—Karthik

Thanks team — we did the first run today during the 8/1 slot. High level findings attached (lab-run-20270801-results.csv). Top takeaways:
- Steady 60m @ 500 rps: p50 TTFT ~85ms, p95 ~320ms — within your stated target for short prompts.
- Spike test: during the 5m peak we saw queue depth increase sharply after ~120s and p95 latency ballooned to ~2.1s for some requests; ~1.3% 429/rejects recorded.
- Context-heavy probe: TTFT for long inputs had higher variance — warm cache runs were ~200ms p50, cold ~620ms p95.
- Notable: a multi-tenant scheduling event on the node was visible (GCE preemption log) that correlated with the largest latency tail.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you recommend server-side rate-limit settings that prioritize TTFT for short prompts while protecting capacity for long-context requests?
2) Do you have a suggested client backoff strategy/queueing guidance to avoid the queue amplification we saw?

Attachments: lab-run-20270801-results.csv; console logs link: https://console.redwood.com/logs/links/brightpay-lab-20270801

Jordan

Subject: Re: MAP: performance lab & action timeline (TTFT / load profiles) — recommendations & next run

Jordan — thanks for the quick lab and the detailed CSV. We reviewed the traces and logs; summary and recommended next steps below. We can run the follow-up on 2027-08-03 09:00 PT if that works.

Analysis summary:
- Queue amplification stems from simultaneous long-context decoding + high client concurrency. The scheduler holds outstanding tokens which increases head-of-line blocking. The GCE event you flagged explains one of the worst tails but does not fully account for the systematic p95 increase during the spike.
- Warm KV cache materially reduces TTFT for long contexts; cache misses add ~350–450ms on average.

Recommendations (short list we’ll implement for the next run):
1) Client-side: set soft concurrency target to 400 total RPS with per-client conn limit of 60. Add randomized exponential backoff for 429s with initial retry delay 50ms up to 1s.
2) Server-side rate-limit: apply a hybrid token-bucket with a burst cap of 2,500 and steady fill of 2,000 tokens/sec; enforce a per-request token cost weighted by context length (>=1 token per 256 prompt tokens) to favor short prompts.
3) Batching / KV: enable prefix KV caching and an aggressive warm-up pass before the main spike window (30m warm-up at 80 rps for long-context paths).
4) Observability: capture scheduler queue depth and per-model inference time on 1s granularity during spike window.

We’ll push a proposed server config (proposed-rate-limit-config.txt) to the drive and run the tuned experiment on 8/3 09:00 PT. If results look as expected we’ll sign off the MAP acceptance criteria and target procurement close by 2027-08-10.

Next steps: confirm 8/3 09:00 PT, we’ll circulate an updated MAP with milestones and acceptance signoff checkpoints.

Attachments: proposed-rate-limit-config.txt
